name: IoT Analytics: Industrial AI and Edge Computing Market Research
title: IoT Analytics: Industrial AI and Edge Computing Market Research
answer: IoT Analytics publishes market research on industrial AI and edge computing, including its 399-page Industrial AI Market Report 2025, 2030. The most useful finding for manufacturers is that the global industrial AI market reached $43.6 billion in 2024 and is forecast to grow at 23% annually to $153.9 billion by 2030, while the average US manufacturer invests only about 0.1% of revenue in AI.

sections.body: IoT Analytics is an independent market research firm whose website carries articles summarising its paid reports on industrial AI, edge computing and the internet of things. The material reviewed spans reports published between January 2025 and May 2026, including the 399-page Industrial AI Market Report 2025, 2030, the 263-page Generative AI Market Report 2025, 2030, a 121-page AI Adoption in Machine Building 2026 report, and event research from Embedded World 2024 and Hannover Messe 2026. The articles mix survey data, vendor analysis and the firm's own market forecasts.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The industrial AI market reached $43.6 billion in 2024 and is expected to grow at a compound annual rate of 23% to $153.9 billion by 2030. Adoption is rising but spending is thin: the average US manufacturer invests roughly 0.1% of revenue in AI, about $40,000 per manufacturer, which is 3% of average research and development spending and 7% of average IT spending. Quality and inspection leads industrial AI use cases, with edge AI, domain-specific industrial foundation models and copilots identified as emerging directions. In machine building, 96% of builders are in some stage of AI implementation and 55% have scaled a use case, though 54% cite high costs as a barrier. Deere & Co. is cited using AI for durability simulation, design concept generation, bill-of-materials cost estimation, vision-based part fitment checks and production sequencing. At Hannover Messe 2026, analysts counted 29 industrial agentic AI solutions, 78% of them model-agnostic, with maintenance and troubleshooting the leading use case.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: IoT Analytics puts the industrial AI market at $43.6 billion in 2024, growing at 23% annually to $153.9 billion by 2030, and the AIoT market at $102.2 billion by 2026. It reports industrial AI adoption rising from 19% to 31% in just over two years, with a further 39% testing or piloting. It identified 634 vendors selling AI technology to manufacturers, 389 of them offering AI software. In generative AI, the market passed $25.6 billion in 2024, manufacturing accounted for 8% of 530 analysed projects, second only to technology at 56%, and NVIDIA held 92% of the data centre GPU market. The firm defines industrial AI as AI related to an industrial enterprise's physical operations and systems, and edge AI as deploying models on equipment at the edge for inference without continuous cloud connectivity.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: This source gives manufacturers a quantified baseline for where industrial AI spending and adoption actually stand, rather than vendor claims. The finding that the average US manufacturer spends about 0.1% of revenue on AI, against 3% of research and development and 7% of IT budgets, frames industrial AI as early and underfunded. The use-case evidence, from quality and inspection leading adoption to Deere & Co.'s design, vision and sequencing applications, shows where value is being realised on the factory floor. The machine building survey and the Hannover Messe agentic AI count give a forward view of what vendors will bring to manufacturers next.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Manufacturing

sections.body: The website presents summaries of commercial reports rather than the reports themselves, so much of the underlying survey methodology and detail sits behind a paywall. Several articles are event-based observations, such as the Hannover Messe 2026 and Embedded World 2024 coverage, which reflect what was shown at trade fairs rather than measured deployment. The generative AI project analysis draws on publicly known projects, which skews toward technology firms and North America. Figures are the firm's own estimates and forecasts, and the material spans multiple publication dates, so readers should check which report each number comes from.
